An ash layer in shale dates to 300 million yrs. The shale above it is…

slides.reveal: Answer: A. By superposition the layer on top is younger (slide 12), and the igneous ash gives a numeric age from radioactive decay (slide 13), so the shale above is younger than 300 million years.

Which list puts Indiana's history in order, oldest first?

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Upper Ordovician and Mississippian seas left the exposed limestone and shale (about 450 to 323 million years ago; slide 19), Pennsylvanian swamps left coal (323 to 299 million years ago on the ICS chart, 318 to 299 by IGWS; slide 20), and glaciers came in the last 2.6 million years (slide 21), from IGWS with period dates from the ICS chart.
